header:
Date: 2027-06-05
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Ava Thompson (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Priya Patel (Head of ML, Seabreeze), Liam O'Connor (CTO), Jun Park (SRE)
summary: Initial discovery focused on model selection for a multi-lingual, long-context document understanding product. Key concerns: 100k-token context support for long documents, multilingual support (EN/ES/JA), tool-calling/function-calling for retrieval plugins, and data residency/security (SOC2, KMS). Explored trade-offs between Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployments and open-model candidates (Mistral, LLaMA-3 variants, Falcon). Agreed on POC to validate 100k token context and latency/cost tradeoffs.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment options
security & compliance: SOC2, KMS/HSM, SSO/SAML, audit logs
model candidates: Mistral, LLaMA-3, Falcon, quantized variants
latency vs cost tradeoffs; batching and KV cache
transcript:
[00:00] Ava (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for jumping on, we really appreciate the time. I'm Ava, AE for this region, and with me is Diego, our solutions engineer. quick quick intro from your side?
[00:18] Priya (Seabreeze): hi, i'm priya, head of ml at Seabreeze, we do document understanding for maritime contracts, lots of very long docs, sometimes 50k to 200k tokens after OCR, so context length is a big deal for us.
[00:31] Liam (CTO): liam here, curious about deployment options, security, and cost.
[00:36] Jun (SRE): jun, i'll be running the POC infra if we go forward. we have on-prem constraints for some customers.
[00:44] Diego (Redwood SE): great, thanks. quick agenda: we want to understand your workload, context length, latency targets, and then go through open-model tradeoffs and Redwood deployment options. sound ok?
[00:57] Priya: yes. we also need strong multilingual support — english and spanish are primary and occasionally japanese. also tool calling, we'll be doing retrieval-augmented generation and some function calls into a search microservice.
[01:15] Ava: perfect, that's helpful. can you give a sense of QPS and latency targets?
[01:21] Priya: at peak maybe 10 qps for end-user-facing endpoints, but batch jobs do run overnight. interactive latency target sub-700ms ideally, but for long context inference we can tolerate a second or two if it keeps accuracy.
[01:38] Diego: awesome. a couple quick clarifying q's — when you say 100k tokens, is that a sliding window with retrieval or full context per request?
[01:46] Priya: it's mostly document-level context — we want to pass the full document plus some retrieval snippets, so sometimes the working set is ~120k tokens.
[01:55] Diego: ok that makes sense. we should note that support for 100k+ context varies by model and deployment. for Hosted we have model variants and special kernel paths that handle longer kv-caches. for Dedicated/Private you get more control — more memory, pinning models, and you can run quantized 4/8-bit workloads if you want cost savings. but there are tradeoffs.
[02:16] Liam: tradeoffs like latency increases with model size? and cost?
[02:20] Diego: exactly. larger context and larger models = more memory and compute. we typically recommend evaluating a few model families: LLaMA-3 style large-context variants, Mistral's larger families which are relatively efficient, and Falcon 40B for specific workloads. some community variants support context extension via chunking + smarter KV cache stitching.
[02:40] Priya: are there open models that already natively do 100k?
[02:44] Diego: native 100k is still bleeding edge — there are experimental LLaMA-3 variants and research forks. in practice we often combine model-level longer context support with prefix-KV caching and retrieval to make it practical. for the POC we can test a dedicated node with a LLaMA-3-extended variant and a Mistral quantized stack to compare quality/cost.
[03:05] Jun: sounds good. one security question — for Dedicated/Private can we integrate our KMS/HSM and have logs?
[03:11] Ava: yes. Dedicated includes customer-managed keys and RBAC; Private (VPC/on-prem) gives full control over KMS/HSM and network isolation. we also provide audit logs and we've got SOC2 plus some ISO assets. i'll share the security whitepaper and SOC2 link after this call.
[03:29] Priya: also SSO — we use SAML with our corporate IDP.
[03:33] Diego: we support S S O and SAML, single sign-on and fine-grained RBAC. sometimes the transcript picks up letters, sorry, but yes SAML + SCIM provisioning for users.
[03:46] Liam: any mention of data residency? we have EU-only customers.
[03:50] Ava: regional hosting options are available for Hosted, and Dedicated can be assigned to regions; Private is fully in your control for residency.
[03:59] Priya: talk to me about tool-calling. we need deterministic function-calls to our retrieval API, and prefer strongly-typed responses for downstream parsers.
[04:08] Diego: Redwood supports function/tool calling and streaming. for deterministic function-calls we recommend using structured function schemas and our streaming mode so you can start processing tokens as they're emitted. we also offer evaluation hooks to assert schema correctness.
[04:25] Priya: perfect. does that work with batching and quantized models? sometimes batching is incompatible with certain tool-calling patterns because you need per-request sync.
[04:34] Diego: good point — batching yields big cost wins but it can increase tail latency. we have dynamic batching and per-route overrides — you can set low-latency routes that avoid batching for interactive calls and batch for background jobs. quantized models are generally compatible but certain int8 kernels have constraints; we'll note that for the POC.
[04:54] Liam: on cost — what's the expected delta between Hosted and Dedicated?
[04:59] Ava: depends on commitment and load. Hosted is easiest: pay as you go with per-token pricing. Dedicated gives predictable throughput and usually lower marginal cost at scale, but requires a commit (monthly/annual). Private has capex/ops tradeoffs. i'll share a pricing sketch.
[05:14] Priya: competitors — have you seen folks doing this with Anthropic or OpenAI?
[05:19] Ava: yes, folks evaluate them. Anthropic has strong safety primitives, OpenAI has good long-context experiments via some partners. we help benchmark side-by-side; Diego can run initial quality tests with your sample dataset.
[05:32] Diego: yes, if you share a representative subset we can run a small benchmark comparing 3-4 candidate models for quality, latency, and cost. we have a benchmark spreadsheet template we usually use.
[05:42] Priya: i'll prepare that. question — do you support on-prem for highly regulated contracts?
[05:48] Ava: yes, Private on-prem is an option. some customers run our private controller in their VPC or air-gapped and we provide an on-prem package. it requires some additional ops work but it's feasible.
[05:59] Jun: ops question — if we do Dedicated and see a spike, is bursting available?
[06:03] Diego: Dedicated supports configurable autoscaling and burst capacity, within contract limits. we also have fallback routing to hosted instances if you want emergency overflow.
[06:14] Priya: about model selection — could you walk through a recommended shortlist for our use case?
[06:19] Diego: sure. shortlist idea: 1) LLaMA-3-xxl-extended / research forks — best for native long context if quality holds, 2) Mistral large family — very cost-efficient, often great multilingual, 3) Falcon 40B for some instruction-heavy tasks, 4) compressed/quantized variants of the above to test price/quality. we should baseline on your dataset — some models do better with legal/maritime corpora.
[06:45] Liam: do you have pre-trained multilingual metrics?
[06:48] Diego: we have internal evals plus some public benchmarks; Mistral tends to be strong in European languages and LLaMA-3 variants have good multilingual footprints. again, baseline on your text.
[06:58] Priya: ok what's the POC look like — timeline and success criteria?
[07:02] Ava: recommend 2-week POC: week 1 data ingestion and baseline runs, week 2 tuning and latency/cost benchmarks. success criteria: >=95% extraction accuracy on our eval set, latency below your SLA for interactive paths (sub-700ms for short context) and demonstrable cost per 1k tokens below target.
[07:22] Priya: acceptable. also want a test for 100k token end-to-end quality — that may take special infra.
[07:29] Diego: for that we'll spin up a dedicated node with increased GPU memory and test extended Kv approaches; it'll be slower but we can measure quality vs chunking+retrieval.
[07:40] Jun: we'll need to sign an NDA for some of the sample data — is that ok?
[07:44] Ava: yes, we can get a standard mutual NDA. i'll follow up.
[07:49] Priya: any showstoppers on our side? we have to validate SAML provisioning, KMS integration, and EU data residency for one of the clients.
[07:59] Ava: all typical enterprise asks — we'll share docs and SOC2. Dedicated or Private handles the KMS/residency aspects.
[08:08] Liam: for evaluation, can you also include cost modeling for quantized vs non-quantized runs?
[08:13] Diego: yes. we'll provide cost estimates using our Optimize tooling — batching, quantization profiles, and spot vs reserved capacity assumptions.
[08:23] Priya: great. one more technical — how do you handle KV cache stitching when chunking a 100k doc? potential for cross-chunk attention loss.
[08:33] Diego: two approaches: 1) naive chunking with retrieval + overlap windows, 2) extended-KV variants that let you stream and stitch caches across chunks. stitching has complexity for attentional ids, but we've built heuristics and testing harnesses. we'll include both in the POC and measure delta.
[08:54] Priya: sounds good. any latency numbers for long-context runs?
[08:58] Diego: depends on model and GPU type. as a ballpark, a single 100k forward on a high-memory A100-style node can be multiple seconds; with optimized kernels and batching it's faster, but still above our short-context SLOs. that's why we measure quality vs cost for retrieval patterns.
[09:17] Jun: what GPUs do you run Dedicated on?
[09:20] Ava: we have pools on modern Ampere and Hopper-class GPUs; for Private you can choose the hardware. we'll include recommended hardware in the POC plan.
[09:30] Priya: ok, are there any limitations on function-calling with streaming?
[09:34] Diego: streaming + function-calling works; we push structured chunks and a final confirmation. caveat: in some quantized kernels you may see variance in token timing; we'll validate in the POC.
[09:46] Liam: what about pricing transparency — I want per-token and slot-level numbers.
[09:50] Ava: we'll share a pricing spreadsheet with sample scenarios — per-token Hosted, Dedicated node cost amortized per throughput, and Private ops estimates.
[09:59] Priya: ok that's great. any references or case studies for long-doc workloads?
[10:04] Ava: yes, i'll link a recent case where a customer processed legal contracts with hybrid retrieval and got a 3x cost reduction vs naive long-model forwards. link in follow-up.
[10:13] Diego: to summarize technical POC steps: 1) receive sample dataset and eval script, 2) run baseline on 3 candidate models (LLaMA-3 variant, Mistral large, Falcon 40B quantized), 3) run extended-context test with dedicated node, 4) measure quality/latency/cost and document.
[10:33] Priya: timeline ok — let's do the scoping call on 2027-06-10.
[10:37] Ava: works for us, diego will lead the scoping.
[10:41] Jun: one more ops micron — how do you handle logs / PII in transcripts? retention settings?
[10:46] Ava: we provide configurable retention and can disable certain logging in Private. Hosted has retention policies and can be configured for enterprise tiers. will include in security doc.
[10:57] Liam: ok, i'm satisfied. any other open questions?
[11:00] Priya: none here.
[11:02] Ava: perfect, we'll follow up with pricing, SOC2, NDA, and a POC scoping invite for 6/10. thanks everyone.
[11:10] (call ends)
